notes: Independent reviewer (scored blind, v2): Facts: every number checks out against the article or at least 2 of its sources. From the article: 2.24 lakh record, 1.51 lakh in Oct 2025, +48.5%, market -28.35% (rounded to 28% on the cover). Not in the article but confirmed by BikeAdvice and Rushlane: TVS No. 1 at 60,490; Ather 31,833; Vida/Hero 29,923; Ola 12,098 vs 16,439; Greaves 10,839; River 6,817; BGauss 5,556; EV share 9.7% (BikeAdvice) and 9.65% (Rushlane 2W), so 'nearly 1 in 10' holds. Bajaj: BikeAdvice gives 49,126 and Rushlane's text gives 49,156, but Rushlane's own TVS+Bajaj total of 1,09,616 and BikeAdvice's table summing to 2,24,064 both imply 49,126, so 'about 49,100' is accurate. The caption credits the Dhanteras/Diwali reason to Rushlane, which is fine because the article itself links the fall to the festive calendar. Framing matches the article's dek. Scores: hook 2 (big +48.5% set against the market falling 28% gives a clear stake). read 2 (every line carries a fact; slide 2's last bullet is a bare list of numbers but still useful data). send 1: this is mainly an industry leaderboard. It gives no buyer or owner takeaway, and the most forwardable point (Ola down 26% while the segment grew 48.5%) sits mid-slide 2 without its percentage, so there is a reason to forward it but no strong one aimed at a specific person. keep 2 (full Oct top-8 brand table, total, YoY, share). reply 2 (one genuine question: 'Is your next scooter or bike going to be electric?'). original 2 (own typographic cards that combine three source articles; sources on both slides and credit line at the end of the caption). alone 2 (the cards make sense without the caption; lakh and the brand names place it in India, and the footer date 10 Nov 2026 places the October; the reason for the market fall is only in the caption, which is a small gap). The render has a defect the score does not capture: slide 2's 'No.' glyph is clipped at the left margin (see legibility/rule problems). Fix that by re-rendering before approval. The render report does not catch it (overflow=false).
scored_as: lower of the two totals (self 13, reviewer 13)
